latest_release.body:
自 v0.19.0 以来，dsh-TUI 跟上 DSH `0.2.2-rc.2` 验证线（同时保留对 `0.2.2-rc.1` 及更早验证线的兼容），
把系统通知扩展到等待授权、等待提问与计划评审，让单栏 Edit/Write diff 按 git hunk 呈现，并修好一批
窄终端重绘、局部压缩摘要与账号通知生命周期问题。

## 亮点

- **适配 DSH `0.2.2-rc.2`** — 主适配线前移到 `0.2.2-rc.2`，peer 范围同时保留 `0.2.2-rc.1`、`0.2.1-rc.5` 等旧验证线，停在上一验证线的用户也能直接装这版。rc.2 上 Agent Teams 改由 `dsh-base` 内置、按会话开关，成员改用具名子代理；账号通知改用新的通知 API（服务器文案卡片、展示/关闭回执、到期与语言刷新）；Search/Fetch 设置拆成独立字段；子代理目录升到 v3（每个子代理带名字与描述）。两代宿主按形状探测而不是按版本门，旧宿主继续走原有 bundle、旧设置表单与旧 bonus API。([#1951](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-TUI/pull/1951)、[#1959](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-TUI/pull/1959) by @Lucas2011wastaken)
- **通知覆盖所有等待状态** — 以前只有任务完成会发系统通知；现在等待工具授权、等待回答的提问与计划评审也会提醒，同一个「通知」开关管四类通知（`/settings` → 对话：`taskNotifications` 默认 `unfocused` 仅失焦，可选 `always` / `off`）。审批正文含会话名、工具名与理由；提问与计划评审只放首个问题的标题与问题，不含选项、详情或整份计划。这些正文来自模型或宿主，已去 ANSI、折叠空白并限长，但**不承诺脱敏**。后台会话与子代理的审批、提问只进面板不提醒；计划评审是唯一不让位给外部通知插件的一类。([#1929](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-TUI/pull/1929)、[#1930](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-TUI/pull/1930)、[#1931](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-TUI/pull/1931) by @Lucas2011wastaken)
- **点击通知回到发起它的窗格** — Windows Terminal 上开启 `jumpBack`（`/settings` → 对话，默认关闭）后，完成、审批、提问与计划评审的 toast 都带「跳回」目标：发送前先做一次只读探测，恰好命中一个窗格或标签标题时才承诺跳回；点击时再核验五项（同一窗格、获得键盘焦点、标题仍含标记、窗口在前台、未最小化），任一步不成立就不动作。无法核验的布局（非 Windows Terminal、`suppressApplicationTitle`、目标在未选中标签等）发普通 toast。开启后每条 toast 约晚半秒，第一条可能等 helper 编译一次。([#1675](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-TUI/pull/1675) by @baobaolaodie；审批/提问/计划评审的接线见 #1929、#1930、#1931)
- **单栏 diff 只显示变更块** — 单栏（unified）的 Edit/Write diff 不再把旧/新全文各铺一遍，而是像 `git diff` 一样只显示变更块与前后各 3 行上下文；行号只来自后端显式给出的真实偏移，没有偏移时不输出 `@@` 头、多个 hunk 之间用 `⋯` 分隔。宽终端（≥110 列）的默认 `auto` 仍走双栏，观感不变。([#1957](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-TUI/pull/1957) by @Lucas2011wastaken)

## 需要留意的行为变化

- **Agent Teams 在 `0.2.2-rc.2` 上的开关方式** — `/team on` / `/team off [force]` 按根会话保存选择，跨重启保持；关闭不停止子代理也不删任务，仍有子代理运行时 `off` 会先提示。旧宿主仍是 `/plugin enable|disable @deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-agent-team-profile`，`/team` 只报告并给出提示。rc.2 移除了 `spawn_teammate` 与 Team 版控制工具，统一用具名 `subagent` / `subagent_fork` / `send_message` / `interrupt_agent` / `list_agents`，旧日志里的旧工具调用仍可读；历史团队会话在 rc.2 投影里没有成员快照，面板退回任务板/子代理视图，恢复出来且没有 live runtime owner 的子会话不再显示 team。
- **共享会话库要一起升级** — `0.2.2-rc.2` 写下的子代理 catalog 是 v3，旧版 DSH 打不开；多个进程共用同一会话库时，把会加载这些会话的 DSH 都升到 `0.2.2` 线再用。
- **通知让位与投递边界** — 外部 DSH 通知插件已启用且 active 时，任务完成、审批与提问让位；计划评审不让位（外部插件只映射审批与普通提问）。原生 toast 排队期间会复检：开关关闭、会话已切换或请求已处理就不再弹出。`jumpBack` 依赖原生 toast 通道（`notificationMethod` = `windows`，本地 Windows 的 `auto` 就选它），真机只在 Windows Terminal 1.24 验证过，更高版本与其他终端按普通 toast 降级。
- **单栏 diff 的行号与超大改动** — 后端没有给出真实位置时只显示变更块、不显示行号；整份文件改写过大时回退成旧的全文行对照。双栏 split 视图与 Codex 的 patch 卡保持原样。
- **DSH `0.2.2` 要求 Node `>=24.9`** — 本包自身仍声明 `^22.19 || >=24`；用更旧的 Node 运行 `0.2.2` 宿主属于上游未支持组合，升级前请先确认 `node -v`。

## 修复

- **渲染与重绘**：inline 主屏在 resize 与空闲重锚定后短帧不再停在终端中部，帧尾贴底（[#1936](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-TUI/pull/1936) by @Lucas2011wastaken）；高于视口的帧收缩后不再在转录与状态栏之间留出空白带（[#1924](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-TUI/pull/1924) by @MomentDerek）；分数宽度下 `truncate` 文本按 1 行测量，窄终端底栏不再凭空多出 6 行空白（[#1922](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-TUI/pull/1922) by @MomentDerek）。
- **压缩摘要**：Live Compact 的 `spine-checkpoint` 局部摘要在实时、回放与会话树中可见，且不会误套全量压缩的上下文组成重置；partial 保留启发式组成，不把摘要大小当净增量（[#1943](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-TUI/pull/1943) by @T-Auto）。插件侧的联合验收在插件仓跟进。
- **账号通知与归属**：关闭卡片会栅栏掉关闭前发起的在途轮询，迟到响应不会复活卡片或重复上报 `displayed`；卡片实际写屏完成后才上报展示，语言变化更新原卡片；子代理与团队按 live owner 归属，恢复出来的 detached 会话不回退猜父队；未 pin 的 Search/Fetch 密钥跟随实际读取的路由；旧宿主与外部内核保持原有 UA 归属（[#1959](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-TUI/pull/1959) by @Lucas2011wastaken）。
- **通知投递**：排队中的 toast 在开关关闭、会话切换或审批/提问/计划评审已处理时取消；关闭后的迟到响应不重新弹卡（#1929、#1930、#1931）。

## 兼容与升级

- **DSH 主适配线**：`0.2.2-rc.2`；`0.2.2-rc.1`、`0.2.1-rc.5`、`0.2.1-rc.4`、`0.2.1-rc.3`、`0.2.1-rc.2`、`0.2.0-rc.2`、`0.2.0-rc.1`、`0.1.7-rc.2`、`0.1.7-rc.1` 以及更早的验证线仍在契约内，契约外版本打漂移警告。
- **npm 上 `latest` 仍是 `0.2.2-rc.1`**：`0.2.2-rc.2` 走 `next` 标签。程序内 `/update` 会在目标 TUI 的 peer 范围内选已发布的最高版本，

detail.readme:
English | 简体中文

# dsh-TUI > An interactive terminal UI for DeepSeek Harness. It ships a pixel-whale > header, live work status, streaming thinking, double-Esc time rewind, a > context progress bar, and a TPS gauge. Zero core changes: it consumes only > DSH's public exports, and is moving from a mounted plugin to an app with its > own entry and composition root, where DSH loads in process as the first-party > backend. Install to enable; uninstall leaves no patches behind. The prompt footer hides completed goals once the turn is idle; the Todo side panel retains their history. `Ctrl+Q` folds todos while working and hides/restores the idle goal/todo footer. Clicking its todo header also hides it while idle. Hiding changes only this display: a new goal/todo snapshot or session reveals it again, and `/goal clear` does not clear todos. Split diff cards give one-sided additions and deletions the full body width, without an empty opposite pane. Ordinary edits remain side by side, and mixed files choose their layout separately before folding or streaming reveal. Compaction status stays on one line in narrow panes: phase and cancellation hints yield first, then the label is shortened; elapsed time is shown only as a complete field. Image files referenced with `@path` use the same admission and resize/conversion policy as pasted images. Adjustment notices report the stored dimensions and format; required animation conversion is refused instead of dropping frames. Mention images and staged images still share count and stored-byte limits in source order. ## Highlights Panels without a verified Component identity are temporary: settings show their title and a distinct number for this run. Their toggles take effect immediately without being saved, and unrelated settings changes preserve that choice. Old `actN:panel` entries cannot be mapped safely: remove the placeholder and select the current panel again. Verified Components named `actN` keep their public runtime address; an explicit selection uses `component:actN:panel` in saved preferences to avoid claiming an old anonymous entry. The default reasoning-effort setting offers the current backend/model’s declared tiers, including custom IDs. Saved values absent from that catalog stay visible and stored; while loading or unavailable, only Auto is selectable. On DSH, Auto follows the saved `/effort` choice, then the configured effort, then the model default. Claude/Codex retain backend preferences for Auto at startup and for resumed sessions; explicitly choosing Auto resets the model default. Explicit settings changes affect the next request; unsupported preferences fall back with a notice and are never forced onto a route. Resuming a DSH session preserves its recorded reasoning effort (or its live selection when reattaching). The saved default seeds new sessions; explicit `/effort` and effort-default settings changes still apply to the current session’s next request. - **Pixel whale pet** — three startup intros, click to wake; freezes after the first task. - **Launchpad and first-run guide** — every ordinary launch lands on a landing page with a **real input box** (big text + whale + quick actions, dropping whole blocks on short/narrow terminals; whale-girl images use a compact native-canvas footprint instead of leaving a large gap before the title; on by default — /settings `launchpad` off boots straight into chat); command completion matches chat: `Tab` fills the input, `Enter` runs the command and clears it. The first run walks a four-step wizard (accounts & models / language+theme / model+workspace / shortcuts), re-runnable with `/setup`; its first step signs in to a subscription and catches the models it brings in (none → no question, one → that one, several → you choose), or adds an API key through the `/provider` wizard, which asks which of the enabled models to switch to or keeps the current one. - **Terminal-native UI** — streaming Markdown, tool cards, `/` and `@` completion, `#L12-14` ranges, history search, zh/en UI. - **Notifications** — one switch covers four system notifications: task completion, a tool approval waiting for your decision, a question waiting for your answer, and a plan review waiting for your decision. Task completion: DSH, Claude and Codex notify after successful live work settles, with no queued follow-up or active goal. The title is “dsh-TUI · Task complete”; the body shows the latest settled reply as a single-line plain-text preview (Markdown formatting removed, up to 200 characters). OSC 777/9 apply an additional 2048-byte sequence budget, including title and protocol bytes, preserving whole graphemes. No reply shows only the title; BEL only rings. `/settings` → Conversation: `taskNotifications` = `unfocused` (default), `always`, or `off`; `notificationMethod` = `auto` (default), `osc9`, `bel`, or `windows`. Auto uses separate title/body fields on Ghostty/WezTerm (OSC 777) and Kitty (OSC 99); iTerm2/Warp and explicit `osc9` use a title prefix; other terminals ring the bell; delivery follows your terminal's notification/bell settings. On local Windows, `auto` resolves to `windows`, the system's native notifications: a task-completion toast. The first toast registers that user's AppUserModelID under HKCU, the toast appears about 3 seconds after the task ends (the PowerShell cold start that buys the no-extra-install route), and for DSH sessions an enabled, active external DSH notification plugin in the running profile makes dsh-TUI yield to it (no toast, no bell); an installed but disabled plugin does not suppress notifications; if that AppUserModelID cannot be written, the notification falls back to the bell instead of going silent. `jumpBack` (Windows, off by default) turns these toasts into a way back to the pane that raised them; it needs the native toast path (`notificationMethod` = `windows`, which `auto` picks on local Windows). With `/settings` → Conversation → `jumpBack` on, the pane title ends with `[dsh-tui:<16 hex>]`, one marker for the life of the process; switching it off removes the suffix at once. While it is on, this process refreshes a marker file at `~/.dsh-tui/notify/jumpback/.json` (`schemaVersion: 1`, `marker`, `pid`, `startedAt`) when the setting is turned on and before each notification it sends, and the first toast that can promise a jump registers the per-user protocol handler (`URL Protocol` plus `shell\open\command`) under `HKCU\Software\Classes\dsh-tui`; a normal exit removes the file, and removes the key once no other live instance still needs it. Only a pre-send probe that finds exactly one target pane (or tab title) puts an activation URI on the toast; clicking it re-runs five checks — same pane, keyboard focus, marker still in the title, foreground window, not minimized — and refuses rather than jumping anywhere else when any of them fails. A click whose target has gone away changes nothing. Layouts that cannot be verified — a pane in an unselected tab that is not that tab's focused pane, profiles using `suppressApplicationTitle`, and terminals other than Windows Terminal (tested on Windows Terminal 1.24) — get a plain toast whose click changes nothing. The probe adds about half a second before each toast; the first one after enabling can also wait for the helper to compile (a few seconds, once), and a machine whose in-box compiler keeps failing retries it at most every five minutes. External notification senders can read the same marker file and point their own toast at `dsh-tui:activate?m=`; the URI and file format are a read-only contract, and this release ships no plugin-side implementation. SSH sessions keep the attached terminal's notification protocol in `auto` mode; explicit `windows` still selects the host's native transport. tmux requires `set -g allow-passthrough on` for OSC notifications and `set -g focus-events on` for focus reporting. Terminals without focus reporting need `always`. Replay, cancellation and failures do not notify. Works in inline and fullscreen modes. A tool approval adds its own notification: the title is “dsh-TUI · Approval needed”; the body carries the session name, the tool name and the asker's reason. The reason is host-provided text (the model's own justification can appear verbatim), so it is normalized to one plain line and length-capped, but the body makes no redaction promise; the tool call's arguments are never read for it. A native toast still being prepared is dropped if the switch turns off, the session is no longer the attached one, or the approval, question or plan review is no longer waiting. Every approval notifies, and only the current session’s does; background sessions and subagents stay quiet. The switch covers all four, so `off` silences approvals, questions and plan reviews along with completions. An enabled, active external DSH notification plugin still makes dsh-TUI yield for completions, approvals and questions; a plan review never yields, and outside local Windows (or in SSH) the existing terminal notification protocol or bell is used. An ordinary question adds its own notification: the title is “dsh-TUI · Waiting for your answer” and the body carries the first question's header and question; options and detail stay in the panel. Local wizard and sign-in questionnaires announce the same way; a subagent's question stays in the panel in this release; the 0.2.2 approval-intent asks are announced the same way as an ordinary question. A plan review is announced as “dsh-TUI · Plan review” and carries the question header and question, never the plan itself, and it is the one notice that does not yield: an external notifier maps approvals and ordinary questions to its own notification but not a plan review, so yielding would leave only its generic idle notice, which never says a plan review is waiting. - **Native cursor** — focused text inputs inherit your terminal's cursor shape, color, blinking, and enabled animation or trail effects in both inline and fullscreen modes. The `/model` picker shows the same cursor during movement between provider tabs, model rows, and effort levels, then hides it after **0.5 seconds at rest**; clipped regions fall back to the model row. The session manager also moves this cursor between the workspace rail, session rows, and search box; typing claims the search caret, and navigation returns it to the focused row. Configure animation and trail effects in your terminal. - **Images** — Kitty/Sixel thumbnails, centered preview with zoom and pan, paste-time fitting, text fallback. Kitty images scale to the reserved cells' physical pixels, including on HiDPI terminals. - **Mermaid diagrams** — ````mermaid ```` fences drawn as Unicode diagrams. - **LaTeX math** — `$…$` and `$$…$$` formulas as Unicode text, fractions and limits stacked in display blocks; `mathRendering: image` typesets block and one-row inline formulas as terminal images on graphics terminals. - **Timeline rail** — every turn clickable; timeline / scrollbar / hidden gutter. - **Side panel** — `Ctrl+B` splits the chat with a panel column once the terminal is wide enough; drag the divider to resize it. All eight built-in panels are enabled by default, and so are plugin panels registered later (`sidePanel.panels: '*'`; untick a row in `/settings` to switch to an explicit list). The header shows each inactive panel's symbol; hover to see its name. Narrow terminals and inline mode keep full-screen panels. In the `todo` panel a long goal wraps to the panel width with its phase on a separate row; when the content exceeds the viewport, focus the panel and scroll with `↑`/`↓` or the wheel (every todo is reachable too) (the compact goal row above the chat input stays a single truncated line with a hover tooltip). - **Live state** — activity animation, context bar, TPS, cache hit rate, effort, tokens, session cost estimate (main + subagents), Git and session metadata. Title, trajectory-strip and session-state animations update independently of the transcript and pause when idle or unfocused. Context-bar fill follows backend occupancy; colors estimate content composition. Compaction clears obsolete estimates, and missing composition displays a single used block with a measured used count in both hover details. - **One session manager** — `/resume` `/home` `/agentview` `/bg` `⌸`. - Live Compact partial checkpoints appear as folded summaries in chat and summary entries in `/tree`; they do not reset the whole context composition. Occupancy follows the host token meter. Folded previews use the durable summary with the same compactionId; expansion retains the complete text, which is also the fallback when the summary event is missing. - **Session workflow** — `/new` `/compact` `/export` `/btw`, model hot-switch, fork, rewind, vim, fullscreen draft editor. `/btw` uses an overlay when its sidebar cannot render. Main-task questionnaires and the fullscreen draft editor take priority while preserving the side question and draft. - **IDE selection channel** — a VS Code selection lands in the prompt. - **DSH integrations** — presets, skills, MCP, goals, todos, subagents, questionnaires. - **Account sign-in** — the standard profile offers pi-ai OAuth for ChatGPT/Codex, Claude, and Grok (plus OpenAI direct and Meta Muse when available), and Host-owned DeepSeek browser sign-in as `deepseek-account` on DSH 0.2.0-rc.1+. Use `/provider` or `/auth` without another plugin. A profile-only update from a global TUI patch that already mounts `dsh-tui-auth` can still start the official loopback callback listener on demand; fixed-port SSH forwarding still requires the global package to be aligned. - **Extensions** — browser interaction, computer use and more. - **Built for long sessions** — event-driven projection, virtualization, bounded caches. Keys and commands: [Interaction and commands](docs/interaction.en.md). Everything else: [documentation index](docs/README.md). Plugin side panels stay enabled when unrelated settings change. Editing the enabled panel list still applies your explicit selection. Workspace side-panel counts match the session manager: the current conversation counts; empty logs, subagents, fork ancestors and archived sessions do not. Registered workspaces with no visible conversations remain at zero. Loading and read errors are shown separately; press `r` to refresh. When a DSH 0.2.1+ Agent moves its session to another directory (the `working_directory` tool or a Git worktree), the status line, Git branch, `@` completion, `!` commands, clicked paths, skill commands and loaded context follow it, including after `/resume`. The session stays registered under the project it started in. Relative paths in cards rendered before a move resolve against the session's current directory when clicked; absolute paths keep their target. Fullscreen mouse selection stays in the pane where the gesture starts, including chat, sidebar and either diff column. Diagonal, word and line selection copy that pane’s text; soft wraps join independently, source newlines remain, and divider drags only resize. ## Preview
## Featured & Listed Among the community plugins recommended by the **official lead of DeepSeek Harness**, dsh-TUI is the first. Featured by the **DeepSeek Harness official WeChat account**, listed in the [dshfind](https://dshfind.com/en/plugins/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-TUI) plugin directory, and ranked **#7 on [GitHub Trending](https://trendshift.io/repositories/146168) daily** (TypeScript).

## Quick Start ### Windows one-click installer (x64) Download `dsh-tui-setup-win-x64.exe` from [Releases](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-TUI/releases) and run it. Per-user, no administrator, fully offline, and no preinstalled Node or DSH. ### Command-line installation Prerequisites: [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en) and [deepseek-harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). The `deepseek-official` API-key route needs `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`. On DSH 0.2.0-rc.1+, the standard profile can instead use `/auth login deepseek-account` and select the separate account route through `/model`. Since DSH `0.2.2-rc.2` it ships inside `dsh-base`: there is no plugin to install and no bundle to enable. It is off by default per root session — `/team on` enables it for this session and its whole subagent tree (the choice survives restarts), and `/team off` switches it off while keeping the subagents and the task board. `/team` (or `/team status`) reports the saved selection, the service and this session's subagents. When subagents are still running, `/team off` asks first (`/team off force`): they keep running — only the task tools and the Team guidance stop. Members are the root session's named subagents: `subagent` / `subagent_fork` take an optional `name` (the root is `lead`, descendants are paths such as `reviewer/checker`) and are the delegation tools — there is no `spawn_teammate` any more. The four `team_task_*` tools are the shared task board. Control tools address agents by name: `send_message({agent, message})`, `interrupt_agent({agent})`, `list_agents` rows `{name, status, description?}`, and `wait_agent` reports `{timedOut}`. Their calls and results render as one-line cards (`send_message` with its target and `sent`, `list_agents` with named rows), and a message between agents as a `✉ ` bubble in the receiving session. The agents dashboard (Ctrl+A) and the agents side panel show a team view: the Lead line, members under their catalog name with `running` / `idle` status, the remaining subagents, a read-only task board (status, owner, `blocked`, write-scope warnings) and a banner when the team record was rejected. A root with Team off still shows its read-only board with a note, and an empty one falls back to the plain subagent view. An older DSH line (`0.2.2-rc.1` and earlier) mounts the retired experimental bundle instead, and TUI keeps that behavior there: the switch stays `/plugin enable|disable @deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-agent-team-profile` (`/team` points at it; a launch without the profile plugin service gets the `dsh plugin --profile dsh-tui add @` CLI route), the durable roster comes from the projection, `spawn_teammate` is the delegation tool (with `subagent` / `subagent_fork` removed while it is present), and disabling the bundle while teammates run asks first. Those packages ship in lockstep with DSH and pin their peers exactly, so the version must match. Limits: on `0.2.2-rc.1` and earlier the switch covers the whole profile, not one session; there is no "enter teammate session" yet, and `/export` leaves team messages out. Upstream limits apply: teammates share one working directory, a team lives in one process, and a task owner is never released automatically. Upgrade every process that opens the same session store together: catalogs written by `0.2.2-rc.2` subagents cannot be opened by older DSH. A delegation provider whose settled runs fail at least twice and at least half the time gets one degraded-channel line above the agents list; the built-in `subagent` route, workflow members and per-type Claude children are excluded because there is no provider to switch to. On native Windows, fragmented Win32 input records are reassembled across short input delays instead of appearing as numeric protocol text. The platform check only reports that this machine might run the private mode (win32-input-mode); a bare `ESC[` fragment is held only after one record has actually been decoded, while a fragment whose own shape is already record-specific holds on its own (which is how even the first record can survive a split). Windows terminals that never enter the mode (mintty, GitBash) therefore keep the classic VT path: a lone `Esc` keeps its normal response time, and a letter typed after a timed-out `ESC[` is not swallowed. Incomplete records are held for a bounded recovery window (1 second from first capture, never extended by later input; 64 bytes max); past either bound the hold ends and input is handled as before. Unrecognized complete CSI sequences are not inserted as text; after a damaged CSI prefix, a bare ASCII letter can be consumed as its terminator, while normal Win32 key records and bracketed-paste text retain their own boundaries. A session's very first record can still leave residue if it is split before its record-specific shape forms; once any record has been decoded, every split position is covered. Inside the recovery window, literal input starting with `[digit;…` cannot be told apart from a protocol prefix — it may be held, or re-joined to a preceding `Esc`. To type it, wait for the window to close, or avoid that shape right after `Esc`. It is then consumed as the reply it completes instead of entering the prompt as protocol text. That claim is evidence-gated, and this is the difference from earlier builds: no query awaiting an answer means nothing is claimed, so a literal `[?61;4c` typed right after `Esc` still enters the prompt exactly as before. The window is bounded like the record hold (about a second, never extended by later input; 64 bytes max); past either bound it ends, and bytes still shaped like an unfinished reply prefix are dropped rather than shown. Inside that window, with a query of the matching response type outstanding, same-shaped literal input can still be claimed as a reply; to type it, wait for the window to close (about a second), or avoid that shape while a query is outstanding. Fragmented SGR mouse reports no longer land in the prompt as text: an incomplete report header is held until the rest arrives, and a report that completes is handled as a mouse event. The hold is armed only while mouse reporting is actually active (fullscreen, with mouse tracking enabled); inline sessions and terminals that never enable tracking keep the existing behavior. The claim window is bounded from first capture (at most 1 second; 64 bytes max), and a continuation arriving inside it is still claimed rather than replayed. Release has no timer: once a parse call sees either bound exceeded, it replays the held bytes as ordinary keys in arrival order — literal input can be delayed, but is never dropped. Picking it in the picker first shows a risk confirmation (`Enter` enables, `Esc` goes back; in fullscreen its Enable / Go back rows are clickable); a typed `/permission auto` switches directly.
